items.question: Do the researchers discuss limitations, threats to validity, assumptions, or scope boundaries?
items.rationale: The paper states scope boundaries for preliminary design, notes manufacturing has not started, and explicitly discusses limitations and future work including the absence of a comparative study.
evidence: Although actual manufacturing of the subsystems has not yet started, comprehensive design activities were undertaken to lay a solid foundation for future development and integration.

It is worth noting that we did not conduct a comparative study of the presented approach versus a traditional one because of budget constraints and the burden of having two different teams working with different approaches.
A comprehensive comparison with the Spiral Model and other iterative approaches was beyond the scope of this paper but is a valuable area for future research.

items.question: Are claimed outcomes explicitly linked to MBSE artifacts, MBSE activities, or model-enabled process changes rather than asserted generically?
items.rationale: Claims about consistency, traceability, rework avoidance, integration, and design validation are explicitly tied to the Capella unified model, Arcadia method, requirement links, and model governance process.
evidence: Using MBSE allows for the systematic integration of various technical, operational, and design aspects, resulting in a more comprehensive conception of the $ ^{3} $ ColStar mission.
The application of the Capella tool and Arcadia method enabled us to ensure that all subsystem designs were integrated and traceable back to the mission's high-level requirements.
Changes in one subsystem's design were reflected in the overall model, allowing for continuous verification and validation of the system's coherence.

bibliographic_review_management.title: Preliminary Design of Satellite Systems through the Integration of Model-Based System Engineering and Agile Methodologies: Application to the 3ColStar Mission

RQ1.rationale: The paper shows how a 1U CubeSat mission, including EPS functions and physical components, can be modeled through Arcadia/Capella abstraction levels, but it does not focus on minimal behavioral knowledge as a research problem.

RQ2.rationale: It claims reliability, consistency, traceability, integration, communication, and schedule benefits from MBSE/agile workflows, but these are mostly system-level rather than EPS-specific and evidence is qualitative.

RQ3.rationale: It describes pre-physical-development validation through Capella traceability, requirements/test-case links, power-budget analysis, thermal/orbital/link analyses, and simulations, but EPS model verification is not the central focus.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Not assessed under the silo rule; this extraction is based only on the supplied metadata and specified paper Markdown.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Address dynamic requirements, interdisciplinary collaboration, traceability/integration issues, documentation overhead, and resource/time constraints in small satellite preliminary design through integrated Agile Systems Engineering and MBSE.
modeling_scope: stakeholder needs and high-level mission requirements
logical architecture of CubeSat, ground segment, actors, and data flows
physical architecture of EPS, OBC, ADCS, communications, payload-related interfaces, thermal and structure connections

power, thermal, communications, and orbit analyses supporting preliminary design
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_level_of_abstraction: Whole 3ColStar mission system including CubeSat, ground segment, mission operations, operations support, IoT ground stations, and space environment; decomposed from operational analysis to system analysis, logical components/functions, and physical components/interfaces.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: Detailed manufacturing, assembly, physical integration/testing, flight operations, formal comparison with traditional or spiral approaches, and open executable model release are outside scope; thermal analysis is explicitly preliminary and uses a lumped single-node model.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Mission objectives, stakeholder needs, operational modes, orbit/contact assumptions, subsystem power consumption, interfaces, and requirements are needed; the paper does not claim fully behavior-free modeling.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.handling_limited_behavioral_knowledge: Arcadia separates problem-space needs from solution architectures, defines logical functions before technology choices, uses iterative sprints and stakeholder feedback to refine requirements, and validates assumptions through power budgets and external simulations before physical implementation.

physical architecture diagrams for EPS, OBC, ADCS, and communications
power budget tables by operating mode

implementation_pathway_tailoring.mapping_to_se_activities_lifecycle_gates: The approach maps Arcadia operational/system/logical/physical architecture work to systems engineering design processes in Pre-Phase A, Phase A, and Phase B; it uses ECSS, NASA NPRs/handbook, JAXA JPAH/J-SSOD constraints, and V-model validation/verification concepts to support preliminary design and later IVVQ.
implementation_pathway_tailoring.approach_classification_rationale: The core is Arcadia/Capella MBSE, enhanced by Agile/Scrum-inspired weekly sprints, subsystem backlogs, centralized governance, and external analysis tools; it is not presented as a complete automated digital thread.
tailoring_rationale: small satellite projects face changing requirements, limited funding/personnel/timescale, and distributed teams
hardware development requires more upfront architecture and validation than software because hardware changes are costly
sequential preliminary design was chosen for validation, risk management, documentation, and configuration management
independent subsystem backlogs were used because each university/organization owned different subsystem expertise
Capella/Arcadia was selected to centralize design decisions and maintain consistency across independently progressing teams

practical_implementation_pathway.rationale: The paper gives a concrete case workflow from requirements and operational analysis to logical/physical architecture, sprint governance, subsystem diagrams, and analysis tables, though implementation/testing remains future work.

toolchain_fragmentation_interoperability.rationale: Capella is positioned as a unified model with links to external tools and analyses, but formal automated interoperability or data exchange among tools is not demonstrated.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: The case explicitly targets a 1U university/government CubeSat with limited resources, distributed institutions, weekly sprints, subsystem backlogs, and preliminary analyses tailored to early design.

governance_project_deliverables_roi_valu.rationale: Section 5.1 details permissions, roles, change authorization, and weekly status meetings; value claims include 4-month design and rework avoidance, although ROI metrics are limited.

newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: The study centers on Agile Systems Engineering for a distributed small-satellite team using weekly sprints, subsystem teams/backlogs, and rapid preliminary design completion.

RQ1: A nanosatellite mission can be modeled from stakeholder needs through Arcadia operational, system, logical, and physical architecture layers in Capella.
EPS can be represented through requirements for continuous power, logical functions for generation/storage/distribution, and physical components such as solar panels, batteries, controllers, and PDU.
The method reduces dependence on early technology choices by defining logical functions before physical architecture, but it still requires mission modes, interface assumptions, and subsystem data.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include technical consistency, coherency, minimized errors, improved communication, traceability, easier integration, avoided rework, shorter preliminary design time, and a more reliable design.
Reliability and integrability claims are linked to unified modeling, traceability, early validation, and change governance, but are mostly qualitative rather than EPS-specific.
Reproducibility is supported by open-source Capella and detailed figures/tables, but limited by unavailable model assets and permission-controlled repository access.
RQ3: Verification procedures are represented through Capella requirement/test-case links, traceability matrices, requirement coverage diagrams, and validation criteria from component to system level.
EPS-related pre-physical verification is mainly power-budget analysis by mode, requirement allocation to EPS components, and cross-subsystem model consistency checks.
The paper reports orbital, thermal, communications/link-budget and power analyses before manufacturing, but no EPS hardware integration or flight validation.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Actual manufacturing of subsystems has not yet started.
Thermal analysis is preliminary and further detailed design analysis is crucial.
No comparative study against a traditional approach was conducted because of budget constraints and burden of parallel teams.
Comparison with the Spiral Model and other iterative approaches was beyond scope and left for future work.
Data availability statement says no new data were created or analyzed and data sharing is not applicable.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: EPS modeling is described in power-budget and architecture terms, but the paper is system-level and not primarily EPS MBSE verification research.
Claimed MBSE benefits lack defect metrics, rework counts, model-check reports, integration-test evidence, or flight/operational data.
Model artifacts are shown as figures but the underlying Capella model/repository is not openly available in the paper.
Interoperability between Capella and external analysis tools is process-based rather than described as an automated digital thread.
Reliability claims are qualitative and not quantified through reliability models or EPS dependability analysis.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: This allowed the digitalization of the system, which was represented by models that contain requirements, architecture, and interfaces between the different parts of the system.

Capella, an open-source MBSE software (version 6.1), facilitated the transition from a traditional document-based approach to a dynamic model analysis and traceability of functionalities throughout the mission.

Requirements were established initially from mission concept, translated into Capella, and linked to various model elements, including operational scenarios, system functions, logical components, and physical designs.
From the component to system level, each part was linked to test cases and validation criteria, enabling systematic verification of compliance with mission objectives.
Traceability: the requirements for continuous power were linked to specific physical components, such as solar panels and batteries, ensuring direct alignment from requirement to implementation.
The power budget computes the power and energy demand; energy generation; storage; distribution, monitoring and control.
The governance structure assigned specific roles and permissions to manage modifications effectively within the unified model.

It is worth noting that we did not conduct a comparative study of the presented approach versus a traditional one because of budget constraints and the burden of having two different teams working with different approaches.

synthesis_consistency.notes_for_consistency_with_lineage: No previous extraction or lineage file was consulted due to the silo rule; supporting tier is retained from supplied metadata.
synthesis_consistency.extraction_confidence_reason: The paper gives detailed mission, MBSE, EPS-budget, and governance information, but many outcome claims are qualitative and some figures are represented only through converted descriptions rather than native model files.
